pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A particle starts from rest and moves along a straight line with a constant acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance traveled by the particle during the 3rd second of its motion is:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Distance in nth second: S_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1). Here u = 0, a = 4 m/s², n = 3. S_3 = 0 + (4/2)(2(3) - 1) = 2 * 5 = 10 m.

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A stone is dropped from a balloon rising upwards with a constant velocity of 10 m/s. If the balloon is at a height of 40 m from the ground when the stone is dropped, the time taken by the stone to reach the ground is (g = 10 m/s²):

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Initial velocity of stone u = +10 m/s (upward). Acceleration a = -g = -10 m/s². Displacement s = -40 m. Using s = ut + (1/2)at²: -40 = 10t - 5t² => 5t² - 10t - 40 = 0 => t² - 2t - 8 = 0 => (t - 4)(t + 2) = 0. Since t > 0, t = 4 s.

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: The position of a body moving along the x-axis is given by x(t) = 2t³ - 9t² + 12t + 5 (in meters). The acceleration of the body when its velocity is momentarily zero is:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Velocity v = dx/dt = 6t² - 18t + 12 = 6(t - 1)(t - 2). v = 0 at t = 1 s and t = 2 s. Acceleration a = dv/dt = 12t - 18. At t = 1 s, a = 12(1) - 18 = -6 m/s². At t = 2 s, a = 12(2) - 18 = +6 m/s².

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A car moving at speed v is stopped by a constant braking force in distance d. If the speed is doubled to 2v while the same braking force is applied, the stopping distance becomes:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Using v² = u² + 2as with final velocity 0: 0 = u² - 2ad => d = u² / (2a). For u' = 2u, d' = (2u)² / (2a) = 4 * (u² / 2a) = 4d.

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A body moves in a straight line such that its velocity is given by v = √(4s + 16) where s is displacement in meters. The acceleration of the body in m/s² is:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: v² = 4s + 16. Differentiating with respect to s: 2v(dv/ds) = 4 => v(dv/ds) = 2. Since acceleration a = v(dv/ds), we get a = 2 m/s².

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A bullet fired into a wooden block loses half of its velocity after penetrating 3 cm. Assuming constant resistance force, the additional distance it will penetrate before coming to rest is:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Let initial velocity be u. After penetrating s1 = 3 cm, v = u/2. Using v² = u² - 2as: (u/2)² = u² - 2a(3) => u²/4 = u² - 6a => 6a = 3u²/4 => 2a = u²/4. For total penetration s until v = 0: 0 = u² - 2as => s = u² / (2a) = 4 cm. Additional distance = s - s1 = 4 cm - 3 cm = 1 cm.

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A vehicle travels half of the total distance with speed v₁ and the remaining half with speed v₂. The average speed of the vehicle for the entire journey is:

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: Total distance = 2d. Time for first half = d/v₁, for second half = d/v₂. Total time T = d(1/v₁ + 1/v₂) = d(v₁ + v₂)/(v₁v₂). Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / [d(v₁ + v₂)/(v₁v₂)] = 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂).

pilotS01AcademicTraces.layer5_QuestionStem: A juggler throws balls into air vertically upward at regular intervals of 1 second. Each ball rises to a maximum height of 20 m. The number of balls in the air simultaneously at any instant (excluding the moments of throwing and catching) is (g = 10 m/s²):

layer6_QuestionSolution.solutionText: For maximum height H = 20 m: u = √(2gH) = √(2 * 10 * 20) = 20 m/s. Total time of flight T = 2u/g = (2 * 20) / 10 = 4 s. Since balls are thrown every 1 s, balls are in air at t = 1 s, 2 s, 3 s (3 balls in air at any given instant).

reconciled675Sample.stem: If vector A = 3î + 4ĵ and vector B = 6î + 8ĵ, then the angle between vector A and vector B is:
reconciled675Sample.solution: Vector B = 2(3î + 4ĵ) = 2A. Since B is a positive scalar multiple of A, the vectors are collinear and in the same direction, so the angle is 0°.

reconciled675Sample.subject: Physics
reconciled675Sample.sourceLocator: Section 4.4, Page 69 (Vector Addition - Triangle and Parallelogram Law)
reconciled675Sample.stem: The resultant of two equal vectors of magnitude P is also equal to P. The angle between the two vectors is:
reconciled675Sample.solution: R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ. Given R = P = Q: P² = P² + P² + 2P² cos θ => P² = 2P²(1 + cos θ) => 1/2 = 1 + cos θ => cos θ = -1/2 => θ = 120°.

reconciled675Sample.subject: Physics
reconciled675Sample.stem: If |A × B| = √3 (A · B), then the angle between vectors A and B in degrees is:
reconciled675Sample.solution: |A × B| = AB sin θ, and A · B = AB cos θ. Given AB sin θ = √3 AB cos θ => tan θ = √3 => θ = 60°.
